ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Megan
Quigley.

From helping people navigate benefits
to asking how systems could serve them better.

≠

Where this question started.

In her work on financial wellness at Lincoln Financial and as a human resources generalist at NBCUniversal, Megan saw people miss support because they did not know it existed, were unsure whether they qualified, or struggled with timing, enrollment, and follow-through.

Available ≠ Accessible grows from those observations. It asks what happens between a policy's promise and a person's experience—and how implementation could make the path easier.

Her experience motivates the question. The national findings come from the public research cited throughout the project.

ABOUT THIS PROJECT

Why this project exists.

This independent project brings together an interactive explanation of benefit access, a practical route to support, and questions for people who design and deliver programs. It is an evidence synthesis, not original national survey research, and it is not affiliated with the programs discussed.
